decisions.answer: R1: It supports content editing by infilling only modified regions, but the paper does not explicitly discuss absence of clicks/pops at edit points, so this is unknown. R2: The minimum viable prompt length for cloning is not specified; prompt-length experiments truncate to 4 seconds, so 3-second feasibility is unknown. R3: It supports cross-lingual zero-shot TTS and style transfer, including speaking other languages in the same voice, so cross-lingual is supported out of the box. R4: It is explicitly described as performing noise removal/speech denoising as a core capability, so it works as a denoiser. R5: It transfers style including emotion and achieves higher MOS and similarity than baselines, indicating relatively expressive, less robotic speech, though fine-grained emotional control is limited.
decisions.notes: R1: Editing mechanism shows frame-level infilling and preserving context but no explicit artifact analysis, so click/pop behavior cannot be confirmed. R2: Cross-lingual prompt-length study uses 4-second truncation; no 3-second or minimum-length cloning guarantee is given. R3: Cross-lingual zero-shot TTS and style transfer are repeatedly claimed, including speaking any language in one’s own voice. R4: Noise removal and speech denoising are listed as supported tasks. R5: Style transfer covers voice, speaking style, emotion, and acoustic condition, and MOS/similarity beat baselines; however, emotion is not independently controllable.
